title: What is known about 1RB1RD_1LC0RF_0LA0RA_1LE1RA_---1LB_0RA0LD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RD_1LC0RF_0LA0RA_1LE1RA_---1LB_0RA0LD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. With p = 0111110, at the right extensions the tape is a list of blocks p^x separated by short separators 0 1^9 0, 0 1^3 0 or q = 0 1^7 0, which behave like digits. The sweeps over 7-cell words are proved in Lean. The blocks grow, shrink and split irregularly; the width grows like 2·√t. The rule is not known.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 66,053 cells have been visited and 47,182 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.531). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.151).

claims.title: Sweep rules
claims.text:
The head sweeps over long runs of a repeated word, rewriting each copy, for any number n of copies and any surrounding tape. Examples:
  • L A> (0101111)^n R → L (1001111)^n A> R
  • L D> (1010111)^n R → L (1100111)^n D> R
  • L D> (1110101)^n R → L (1111001)^n D> R
  • L F> (0111101)^n R → L (0111110)^n F> R
Generated by py/rules.py (tools/py/bbtools/symtm.py).

claims.title: Square-root width
claims.text: The width is 72,388 at step 1.36·10<sup>9</sup> and 147,106 at step 5.61·10<sup>9</sup>, about 2·√t.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The decider pipeline of bbchallenge left it open; no proof either way is recorded here yet.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LF_0RC0LC_1LA1LD_1RE1LC_---1RA_0LC0RD up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 66,053 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Blocks and digits
html:
Write p for 0111110. At step 5,607,797,795, with the head in A at the right end, the tape is

p 0 1^9 0^2 1^9 0^2 1^9 0 p^7782 0 1^3 0 p^3734 0 1^3 0 p^4744 0 1^9 0 p^2189 0 1^9 0 p^27 0 1^9 0 p^1381 0 1^9 0 p^993 0 1^9 0 p^150 0^2 A>

Long blocks of p separated by one of a few separators: 0 1^9 0, 0 1^3 0, and at other times 0 1^7 0. The sweeps rewrite the tape seven cells at a time (the Lean rules).

sections.heading: How the list changes
html: The separators act like digits of a counter whose blocks keep growing, but how a round trip changes the separators and the blocks is not known. A halt (E reading 0) has not occurred in 6·109 steps.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.531). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.151).
After 109 steps the tape spans 66,053 cells (49,910 left of the start, 536 right), with a density of 1s of 0.714.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB0LF_0RC0LC_1LA1LD_1RE1LC_---1RA_0LC0RD: rename A→C, B→A, C→B, D→D, E→E, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state B, in a mirror

summary: A list of blocks of 0111110 separated by digits 0 1^9 0, 0 1^3 0 or 0 1^7 0, rewritten by 7-cell sweeps; block sizes change irregularly (7782, 3734, 4744, 2189, 27, 1381, 993, 150 at step 5.6*10^9) and the width grows like 2*sqrt(t). Counter-like with several digit kinds; halting open.
family: block counter with several separator digits
